title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less
abstract: arXiv:2609.05370v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Decompilation recovers high-level source from compiled machine code and serves as a foundation for security tasks such as vulnerability detection and malware analysis. Traditional decompilers like Ghidra and Hex-Rays expose whatever they cannot resolve as visible placeholders and often emit pseudocode that will not compile or execute; LLM-based decompilers produce clean, idiomatic C and are now judged almost entirely by recompilability and re-executability: whether the output builds and passes its shipped input/output tests. We show that these metrics can reward the wrong path: a function may recompile and pass every shipped test yet diverge on other legitimate inputs, and a disclosed vulnerability may disappear from the recompiled code with no visible trace of the crash. Neither failure is caught by existing suites.   To address this gap, we propose Decompile-Diverge, a behavioral comparison oracle not relying on fixed or hand-crafted

translated_title: 当LLM反编译器重编译得更多而保留得更少时
translated_abstract: 反编译技术从编译后的机器代码中恢复高级源代码，是漏洞检测和恶意软件分析等安全任务的基础。传统反编译器（如Ghidra和Hex-Rays）会将其无法解析的内容以可见占位符的形式暴露出来，且常常生成无法编译或执行的伪代码；而基于LLM的反编译器能生成干净、符合习惯用法的C代码，如今几乎完全以可重编译性和可重执行性来评判其质量：即输出代码能否构建成功并通过其附带的输入/输出测试。我们证明这些指标可能会“奖励”错误的路径：一个函数可能成功重编译并通过所有附带的测试，但在其他合法输入上却产生行为分歧；同时，一个已披露的漏洞可能在重编译后的代码中消失，且没有任何崩溃痕迹。现有的测试套件都无法捕捉这两种失败。为了解决这一空白，我们提出了Decompile-Diverge，一种不依赖于固定或手工构建的行为比较判定方法。
tldr: 该论文揭示了以可重编译性和通过附带测试作为LLM反编译器评估标准的局限性——反编译代码可能在其他输入上产生行为分歧甚至悄然消除已披露漏洞——并提出了一种名为Decompile-Diverge的行为比较判定方法来弥补这一评估空白。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that recompilability and test-passing metrics can mask behavioral divergence in LLM-decompiled code—including the silent disappearance of disclosed vulnerabilities—and proposes Decompile-Diverge, a behavioral comparison oracle, to address this evaluation gap.
